central_topic: Finite-budget memorization without observed delayed generalization in width-scaled one-hot ReLU MLPs on modular addition and subtraction, comparing AdamW decay arms and shared constant versus exponential learning-rate schedules.
core_methods: Concatenated one-hot input pairs and a two-layer ReLU MLP with hidden widths 16, 64 and 256
Full-batch AdamW with weight decay 0 or 1
Shared seed-independent constant learning rate 0.01 versus exponential schedules with the same initial rate and decay factors 0.5 or 0.1
Sustained train/heldout accuracy crossings with a finite 20000-update observation horizon; checkpoint losses, weight norms and prediction controls
comparators: Original grokking on small algorithmic datasets
Weight-norm and loss-landscape explanations of grokking
Circuit-efficiency explanations of grokking, as untested mechanistic comparators
Lazy-to-rich training dynamics, as an untested two-layer-network comparator
Grokking and model-size or epoch-wise double descent, without asserting an observed double-descent curve
Training-set fitting versus generalization and explicit regularization
Decoupled weight decay and its learning-rate-dependent cumulative shrinkage
benchmarks: Synthetic modular addition and subtraction modulo 97; each operation has 9409 possible ordered input pairs
Hash-partitioned search and final subsets; each final operation has 1411 training pairs and 3294 heldout pairs, not a standard named benchmark split
result_driven_themes: Recorded final traces contain zero sustained heldout-accuracy crossings in 36 cases across three seeds, despite sustained memorization in 30 cases; this is finite-horizon non-observation, not proof that grokking cannot occur
Width affects recorded memorization timing, but with every generalization time censored, the reported lag contrast does not identify a change in generalization time
The constant-rate recipe ranks above both annealed recipes on the recorded search aggregate; no paired significance or causal explanation follows from that ordering
Learning-rate changes also change cumulative AdamW shrinkage, so scheduling and regularization effects are not isolated
Recorded negative control gaps warrant separating training fit from learned heldout algorithmic behavior; the controls are not random-label training experiments

queries.query: "Grokking: Generalization Beyond Overfitting on Small Algorithmic Datasets" 2201.02177
queries.rationale: Task-provided starter entry 1 defines the relevant small algorithmic/modular-arithmetic setting and delayed-generalization phenomenon. Needed to distinguish that phenomenon from the present recorded absence of generalization crossings within 20000 updates. Do not import its architecture or split into this run.

Task-provided starter entry 11 directly grounds the implemented AdamW optimizer. Both decay arms and all learning-rate recipes alter the update/shrinkage balance; the recipe comparison does not hold cumulative decay fixed.

Task-provided starter entry 3 supplies the weight-norm/loss-landscape comparator relevant to recorded norm, train-loss and heldout-loss traces. No norm intervention or norm-based causal explanation was established here.

Task-provided starter entry 4 is an expected alternative explanation for memorization followed by algorithmic generalization. Cite as a mechanistic comparator only: these experiments contain no circuit extraction or circuit-efficiency measurement.

queries.query: "Grokking as the Transition from Lazy to Rich Training Dynamics" 2310.06110
queries.rationale: Task-provided starter entry 5 provides a two-layer-network dynamics comparison appropriate to the fixed two-layer MLP family. Its regression setting and dynamical claims must not be treated as demonstrated for this classification run; no lazy-to-rich transition was measured.

Task-provided starter entry 6 links the grokking literature to interpolation-related generalization phenomena. Relevant to separating memorization from delayed generalization when all recorded generalization times are censored, not evidence that this run exhibits double descent.

queries.query: "Deep Double Descent: Where Bigger Models and More Data Hurt" 1912.02292
queries.rationale: Task-provided starter entry 10 anchors the distinct model-size and training-duration comparator expected for a width sweep. Keep separate from the grokking-specific unification paper; three widths and no generalization crossings do not establish a double-descent curve or interpolation threshold.

Task-provided starter entry 9 contextualizes the observed separation between training-set fit and heldout performance, and the regularization comparison. Its image/random-label experiments are external context, not controls performed in this run.
